title: The Stock Market Just Flashed a Warning Signal That’s Been Right 83% of the Time Since 1960. Here’s My Plan.
author: Matt Dilallo
description: Margin debt has surged 49% year-over-year, a warning signal that has preceded market declines 83% of the time since 1960. In response, the author is adopting a defensive investment strategy focused on high-quality dividend growth stocks, particularly through the Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF and individual positions like Procter & Gamble, while building cash reserves for potential market opportunities.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Recommended as a core defensive holding offering 3% yield with 100 high-quality dividend stocks that have grown dividends at 9% annually. Low expense ratio (0.06%) and strong historical performance with lower volatility make it suitable for cautious market conditions.

Highlighted as an ideal defensive holding with 70 consecutive years of dividend increases (Dividend King status), durable revenue, attractive valuation, and 2.8% yield. Author recently added it to portfolio despite existing SCHD exposure, citing its ballast during downturns and long-term upside potential.

title: History Says This Is Hands-Down the Best ETF to Buy if a Bear Market Is Coming
author: Ben Gran
description: With concerns about a potential bear market, the article recommends the Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD) as a defensive investment strategy. Based on 2022 bear market performance, defensive sectors like healthcare, consumer staples, and energy outperformed tech-heavy indexes. SCHD holds 102 stocks with minimal tech exposure (9.23%) and heavy weighting in defensive sectors, making it suitable for portfolio protection during economic downturns.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Recommended as the primary investment choice for bear market protection. Features low expense ratio (0.06%), strong historical returns (13.1% annualized since 2011), and outperformed broader indexes during 2022 bear market. Well-positioned with defensive sector allocation.
Highlighted as a top holding in SCHD and exemplifies well-established companies with strong balance sheets that maintain profitability and dividends through economic cycles.
Mentioned as a household name holding in SCHD representing stable consumer staples companies that perform well during recessions.
Cited as a pharma giant holding in SCHD, representing healthcare sector defensive characteristics that maintain strong performance during bear markets.

title: Want to Retire on Dividends? Here Are 4 Stocks to Buy Now and Never Sell.
author: John Ballard
description: The article recommends four consumer staples companies as long-term dividend investments: Procter & Gamble, Coca-Cola, Colgate-Palmolive, and Hershey.
